emma_sec: heads up — main branch had a SAST critical that blocked a deploy but our KMS audit doesn't show a decrypt entry for the build service account. wondering if ephemeral KMS tokens are rolling over before logs are emitted? :thinking:
prashant_eng: saw that alert earlier. CI log shows failure at the artifact decrypt step, exit code 1, then retried and succeeded after ~30s. build job used ephemeral key material from keystore-service.
prashant_eng: snippet from CI:```
ERROR: decrypt failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = request denied
# retry: gcloud kms decrypt --key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/deploy-key ...
```
mike_sre: @prashant_eng can you paste the full build job yaml? I want to check if the job is doing a short-lived grant with TTL < 1m. If so, audit logs might not record the grant creation before the decrypt attempt.
prashant_eng: here's the relevant GH action step:```yaml
- name: Decrypt artifacts
  uses: google-github-actions/auth@v0
  with:
    workload_identity_provider: projects/123/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/redwood-pool/providers/gha
- run: gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file=enc.tar.gz --plaintext-file=plain.tar.gz --key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/deploy-key
```
lisa_prodsec: two quick asks: (1) we need a safer pre-merge gating policy for any SAST/DAST critical that ties an approval to a recorded KMS decrypt event, and (2) the security-service account needs a read entry in audit logs (not just owner perms) so we can always reconstruct timeline.
emma_sec: Agreed. Proposal: add a check in the premerge pipeline that fails the PR if a recent deploy-to-branch run shows a SAST critical without corresponding "protoPayload.methodName=google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" entry in logs for the service account that attempted the decrypt. If missing, require manual approval from security.
mike_sre: we can implement a lightweight log-check action. Example gcloud command to validate audit log presence:```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_cluster" AND protoPayload.methodName="google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND resource.labels.project_id="redwood"' --limit 1 --project=redwood-prod --format=json
```
If it returns empty, fail the check.
prashant_eng: we should also avoid brittle timing windows. suggestion: change the grant TTL to >= 5m for deploy-time ephemeral creds and add exponential retry with jitter for decrypt to tolerate short propagation delays.
cicd-bot: [auto] created issue #SE-487: "Premerge: verify KMS decrypt audit entry for SAST-critical PRs" — assigned to @emma_sec, priority P2. Link: https://github.internal/redwood/security/issues/SE-487
lisa_prodsec: thanks @cicd-bot. @emma_sec can you own the policy update? I'll draft the audit log query and required RBAC change. Specifically we need to grant roles/cloudkms.viewer (or the smaller cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter) to the ci-audit-reader service account and ensure Cloud Audit Logs export retention is >= 90d.
emma_sec: I can own the policy. Next steps: (1) PR to GH actions adding the log-check action + 5m TTL recommendation, (2) infra ticket to bump grant TTL and add the service account role, (3) ops runbook update that says: when a SAST critical blocks with missing decrypt log, escalate to sec oncall and include the gcloud logging read output. I'll open PRs today. :+1: 
prashant_eng: adding a tiny improvement: make the log-check action tolerant — allow a 30s window after the last attempt before declaring missing logs, so transient races don't create noise.
mike_sre: SGTM. If anyone needs my help with the GH action or the gcloud query, ping me. I'll also add a small tracer in runtime to emit a structured marker before decrypt so we can correlate. :eyes:
emma_sec: perfect — I'll update SE-487 with the checklist and mark owners. I'll ping when PR is up.
